card.title: What a roulette bet is really worth

body.question: In American roulette (38 pockets), you bet $1 on a single number. It pays $35 if you win. On average, what happens to each $1 you bet?
body.reveal: You lose about 5 cents. A win has a 1 in 38 chance and pays $35, so the expected result is -$1 x 37/38 + $35 x 1/38 = -$1/19. Expected value is the average outcome if you could repeat the bet many times.

probes.question: What does the expected value of a bet describe?
options: The average result if repeated many times

probes.question: True or false: a single-number roulette bet in American roulette has a negative expected value for the player.

claims.quote: The roulette game consists of a small ball and a wheel with 38 numbered pockets around the edge.

claims.claim: $1 single-number bet wins with probability 1/38 and pays $35
claims.quote: the payoff is $35; otherwise the player loses the bet

claims.claim: Expected result is -$1 x 37/38 + $35 x 1/38 = -$1/19, about -5 cents per $1
claims.quote: Thus, in 190 bets, the net loss will probably be about $10.

claims.claim: Expected value is the average outcome if repeated many times (probe)
claims.quote: the expected value can be interpreted as the long-run average of results from independent repetitions of the same random experiment

claims.claim: Single-number bet has negative expected value (probe true)
